title: Match or create with MERGE
summary: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing.
introduction: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing. Your task: Run the query twice and check the number of matching ids.
learningObjectives: Run the query twice and check the number of matching ids.
Explain the example for match or create with merge

blocks.text: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing. Merge on a stable key, then SET fields that may change.
Use Neo4j 5+ locally with Neo4j Browser or another Cypher editor. These queries use fictional cma-prefixed ids. Cypher is not SQL and does not run in this site's SQL playground.

blocks.code: MERGE (b:Book {id:'cma-b2'}) SET b.title='Garden Days',b.pages=40 RETURN b.title;
blocks.title: Match or create with MERGE

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `MERGE` matches or creates the specified graph pattern. Use a stable identity pattern, then SET changing properties.

blocks.text: The book with id cma-b2 is created or updated with the title Garden Days.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Putting a changing title into the MERGE key pattern can create unintended new nodes. Keep identity separate from changing facts.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Run the query twice and check the number of matching ids.
